top_story.headline: General Services Administration plans another no-bid security upgrade at the White House Complex
top_story.dek: The agency says Convergint Technologies LLC is the only responsible source for design-build work on system headends at the White House Complex and Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling.
paragraphs: A justification posted October 7 by the General Services Administration says the agency plans to hire Convergint Technologies LLC for design-build services to upgrade existing system headends at the White House Complex and at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling in Washington, D.C. Listed sites include the Eisenhower Executive Office Building, the New Executive Office Building, the Winder Building and 726 Jackson Place Northwest. The contract value is redacted.

The agency calls it a logical follow-on to a design-build contract awarded to Convergint in 2020 and completed in 2024, and cites the firm's security clearance and experience in the White House Complex. It invokes the only-one-responsible-source exception to competition, and the document describes the current system as facing planned obsolescence. The agency also posted a sole-source justification for DJB Contracting, Inc to replace the historic balcony on the Winder Building.

sections.headline: General Services Administration plans another no-bid security upgrade for the White House Complex
paragraphs: 42 new sole-source justifications and 921 new solicitations; 86 notices already covered in earlier editions are not repeated.

blocks.title: General Services Administration picks Convergint again, without competition, to upgrade security systems at the White House Complex
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The agency's Public Buildings Service plans a design-build contract to upgrade system headends at the White House Complex, nearby Washington buildings including the Eisenhower Executive Office Building and New Executive Office Building, and Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling. It calls the award a logical follow-on to a 2020 contract with the same firm that finished in 2024, citing the firm's existing security clearance and White House experience and the planned obsolescence of the current system. The justification is dated May 20, 2026 and was posted October 7.

blocks.title: Education Department extends $81.4 million in attorney work on student-loan borrower defense claims without competition
meta: logical follow-on under a Federal Supply Schedule order
blocks.text: Two task order modifications (91003126F0014 and F0015) for Federal Student Aid would keep contract attorneys adjudicating borrower defense applications. The department says 144 contractors are already onboarded and trained, and that stopping to compete the work would lose that investment and disrupt progress toward zero backlog by 2028. The justification is posted in two parts.

blocks.title: Air Force gives Leidos a sole-source bridge on its Medusa counter-drone software while the long-term contract is competed
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The bridge covers engineering and integration support for the Medusa counter-small-unmanned-aircraft command-and-control system. The document says the bridge keeps support running while the government completes competitive source selection for the long-term follow-on, and that Leidos, as the incumbent developer, has unique knowledge of the software architecture, hardware configurations and subsystem interfaces. It was signed September 23, 2026.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement keeps Steampunk on its Visa Security Program tracking system through a sole-source interim contract
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The new interim contract, issued under Steampunk's existing governmentwide IT contract, covers operations and maintenance of the Visa Security Program Tracking System, including its Amazon Web Services GovCloud hosting and help desk. The agency says uninterrupted operations, the incumbent's operational knowledge and avoiding transition delays and duplicate costs justify skipping competition.

blocks.title: Army hires BAE Systems for $4.1 million in training support tied to the Ukraine Management Office, with no competition
meta: BAE Systems Land and Armaments L.P.
only one company can do it
blocks.text: Army Contracting Command – Detroit Arsenal proposes a new service contract for field service representatives to deliver training and training support for the Advanced Mechanic Institute 2.0 outside the continental United States, supporting the Ukraine Management Office. The total estimated price is $4,094,268.

sections.headline: Four spend plans updated across DHS, State, and Education as agencies adjust budgets
paragraphs: No new apportionment files were flagged this window, but four existing spend plans were updated. U.S. Department of Homeland Security revised plans for Immigration and Customs Enforcement facilities and Coast Guard operations, while U.S. Department of State submitted an updated congressional notification reflecting recent reorganization and hiring policy changes, and U.S. Department of Education updated its multiyear education spending priorities.

blocks.text: DHS Immigration and Customs Enforcement's FY2026 Facilities and Improvements spend plan was revised to reflect a $260.9 million portfolio of detention and enforcement facility projects across multiple states. The updated plan details construction and renovation work including a $32 million processing center dormitory in Miami, facility expansions in El Paso totaling $45 million, and training facility construction at Fort Benning, Georgia. Spend Plan.

DHS U.S. Coast Guard's Operation and Support spend plan was updated with minor revisions to field operations funding allocations for depot maintenance and autonomous maritime systems across surface, air, and shore facilities. Spend Plan.

U.S. Department of State's Diplomatic Engagement spend plan was updated via congressional notification from Paul D. Guaglianone, Senior Bureau Official, documenting $10.5 billion in total resources across diplomatic programs and operations. The updated plan reflects impacts of a January 2025 hiring freeze, a Deferred Resignation Program affecting 258 employees with $50.6 million in salary savings, and closure of the R/Counter Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Hub. The plan also notes ongoing contract and grant review directed by Executive Order 14222, with further savings expected for FY2026. Spend Plan.

U.S. Department of Education revised its multiyear spend plan for Safe Schools, Citizenship Education, Innovation and Improvement, and Higher Education programs. The plan allocates $168 million for the Fund for the Improvement of Postsecondary Education, $259 million for Education Innovation and Research, $211 million for School Safety National Activities, and $150 million for Full-Service Community Schools. Spend Plan.
